course.title: Relational Database Modeling and SQL
course.description: This course provides an in-depth introduction to the principles, design, and implementation of Database Management Systems (DBMS). It explores the fundamental concepts of data organization, data models, database architectures, and the characteristics that distinguish the database approach from traditional file-based systems. Students will learn to analyze data requirements, model data using the Entity–Relationship (ER) model, and transform conceptual designs into relational database schemas. The course also covers database languages and interfaces, with a strong emphasis on Structured Query Language (SQL) for data definition, manipulation, and retrieval. Through lectures, practical exercises, and projects, students will gain hands-on experience in creating and managing relational databases, enforcing data integrity, handling transactions, and understanding database constraints. Topics also include database system architectures, classification of DBMSs, and key operations such as INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE, and complex retrieval queries. In addition to technical proficiency, the course emphasizes teamwork, communication, and ethical considerations in data management. Students will develop problem-solving and analytical skills essential for designing efficient, secure, and scalable database systems that meet organizational and user needs. By the end of the course, learners will be prepared to apply database concepts and technologies in real-world applications and data-driven environments.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction and An Example, Characteristics of the Database Approach.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the purpose and importance of database systems. LLO2: Differentiate between file-based and database approaches. LLO3: Identify key characteristics of the database approach.

topics.title: Topic 2: Advantages of Using the DBMS Approach, When Not to Use a DBMS.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Discuss the main advantages and limitations of DBMSs. LLO2: Evaluate situations where a DBMS is or is not appropriate. LLO3: Recognize ethical and organizational factors in database adoption.

topics.title: Topic 3: Data Models, Schemas, and Instances.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define data models, schemas, and instances. LLO2: Distinguish among levels of data abstraction. LLO3: Explain the concept of data independence.

topics.title: Topic 4: Database Languages, Interfaces, and system environment.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe different types of database languages (DDL, DML, DCL). LLO2: Explain DBMS interfaces and components. LLO3: Illustrate how users interact with the DBMS environment.

topics.title: Topic 5: Centralized and Client/Server Architectures for DBMSs.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe centralized, client/server, and distributed DBMS architectures. LLO2: Compare architectural models and identify their advantages. LLO3: Compare architectural models and identify their disadvantages.

topics.title: Topic 6: Classification of Database Management Systems.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Classify different types of DBMSs (hierarchical, network, relational, NoSQL, etc.). LLO2: Discuss use cases for each DBMS type. LLO3: Compare their advantages and disadvantages of DBMS.

topics.title: Topic 7: Data Modeling Using the Entity–Relationship (ER) Model.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify entities, attributes, and relationships from a case study. LLO2: Construct an ER diagram representing user requirements. LLO3: Apply normalization concepts in the modeling process.

topics.title: Topic 8: Entity Types, Entity Sets, Attributes, and Keys.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Differentiate types of entities and attributes. LLO2: Identify and assign primary and foreign keys. LLO3: Apply key constraints in ER modeling.

topics.title: Topic 9: Relationship Types, Relationship Sets, Roles, and Structural Constraints.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define relationships and their properties. LLO2: Interpret cardinality and participation constraints. LLO3: Model complex relationships using ER notation.

topics.title: Topic 10: Relational Model Concepts, Constraints and Relational Database Schemas.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain relational model components (tables, tuples, attributes). LLO2: Convert an ER model into a relational schema. LLO3: Apply relational integrity and key constraints.

topics.title: Topic 11: Update Operations, Transactions, and Dealing with Constraint Violations
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Perform update, insert, and delete operations. LLO2: Explain the concept of database transactions. LLO3: Identify and handle constraint violations ethically and technically.

topics.title: Topic 12: Basic SQL, SQL Data Definition and Data Types
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Create database structures using SQL (CREATE TABLE, ALTER, DROP). LLO2: Define appropriate Key. LLO3: Define appropriate data types and constraints.

topics.title: Topic 13: Basic Retrieval Queries in SQL
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Write SQL SELECT statements for data retrieval. LLO2: Use filtering, sorting, and grouping clauses. LLO3: Perform simple and nested queries.

topics.title: Topic 14: INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE Statements, Additional Features of SQL
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Manipulate data using INSERT, DELETE, and UPDATE. LLO2: Apply advanced SQL features such as views and indexes. LLO3: Collaborate in a group project to design and implement a complete database solution.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
